text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Indictment in attorney general scandal likely - report.
- Foreign minister's cronies get top envoy jobs.
- President Weizman to host Queen in Diana's old home.

- Motorola Inc of Illinois and Israel's Emultek announced recently they have received a $1.1 million allocation from BIRD foundation for $3 million joint project to enhance Emultek's "Rapid" tool for virtual prototyping.
- ESC Medical Systems Ltd recently announced agreement to acquire Luxar Corporation, designer and manufacturer of surgical and cosmetic lasers for undisclosed sum.

- Siemens AG has decided not to establish a new company in Israel to handle machinery sales because too much investment required; Siemen's computer support and energy-related equipment will continue to be handled by Siemens Israel.
- Teledata authorises seconday public offering; has filed a registration statement with Securityes and Exchange Commission; up to 1.1 million ordinary shares expected to be sold.
- Nice Systems, provider of computer telephony equipment and IBS Corp, privately held U.S. company, announced joint project to provide voice and data evaluation tool for U.S. call centre.
HAARETZ
- Police think there is basis for indictments in the scandal over appointment of attorney general.
- Pentagon says it taking seriously allegations that U.S. engineer gave information on U.S. military to Israeli officers.
- Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon: Israeli army killed shepherd.
- Bank workers strike today.
- Jewish man who spit on ground as procession carrying cross went by is convicted in court of interfering with worship; his appeal of conviction rejected.
- Haaretz has learned Tempo drinks company to fire 11 percent of workers, 150 people.
- Netanyahu says Bank Hapoalim will have to give up some assets in framework of its sale.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu: We'll build in all of Jerusalem without limit -- and in Har Homa area of Arab East Jerusalem.
- Survey: 46 percent back building in Har Homa, 29 percent oppose, 25 percent don't know; based on 497 Jewish Israeli adults.
- Soldier arrested after telling people officer who stopped soldier who shot up Hebron market in January should be killed.
- Treasury experts estimate first quarter deficit will reach 3.5 billion shekels well over one billion deficit plannned.
- ESC acquires Luxar for shares worth $93 million.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Former lawyer of politician Deri on attorney general scandal: Deri threatened Netanyahu via me.
- Sephardi chief rabbi demands investigation into selling of conversions.
- Member of Ivri commission on helicopter disaster in which 73 soldiers died wants to question air force chief.
- Family of U.S. woman killed in attack in Gaza two years ago sues Iran for compensation.

- Survey on building new neighbourhood for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem: 38 percent want to building now, 31 percent prefer to wait for appropriate time, 24 percent against building. Surveyed 508 Israeli citizens.
